answer.short_answer: Ji haan, agar kisi muahiday (agreement) ka consideration ya maqsad (object) unlawful ho, to woh muahida void hota hai.
answer.explanation: Contract Act, 1872 ke mutabiq, har woh muahida jiska consideration ya maqsad unlawful ho, void qarar diya jata hai. Unlawful consideration ya maqsad mein woh cheezein shamil hain jo qanoon se mana hon, kisi qanoon ki khilaf warzi karti hon, fraudulent hon, kisi ko nuqsan pohanchati hon, ya jinhein adalat immoral ya public policy ke khilaf samjhay.

citations.quote: Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.
Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found

Yes, you may demand the return of a gratuitously lent item at any time, but you must indemnify the borrower if the premature return causes them a loss that exceeds the benefit they derived from the loan.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, a lender can reclaim a gratuitously lent item even if a specific duration was agreed upon. However, if the borrower has acted in reliance on that duration and suffers a loss exceeding the benefit they gained from the loan, the lender is legally required to compensate the borrower for the excess loss.

citations.quote: The lender of a thing for use may at any time require its return, if the loan was gratuitous, even though he lent it for a specified time or purpose. But, if, on the faith of such loan made for a specified time or purpose, the borrower has acted in such a manner that the return of the thing lent before the time agreed upon would cause him loss exceeding the benefit actually derived by him from the loan, the lender must, if he compels the return, indemnify the borrower for the amount in which the loss so occasioned exceeds the benefit so derived.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, agar aap muahiday (agreement) ki khilaf warzi karte hue kisi cheez ko istemal karte hain aur us se nuqsan hota hai, to aap us nuqsan ka harjana bharnay ke zimmedar hain.
answer.explanation: Qanoon-e-Muahida Act, 1872 ke mutabiq, jab koi muahida tora jata hai, to mutasira fareeq us nuqsan ya zarar ka muawza (harjana) wasool karne ka haq rakhta hai jo us khilaf warzi ki wajah se paida hua ho.

citations.quote: جب کوئی معاہدہ توڑ دیا گیا ہو، تو وہ فریق جو اس نقص معاہدہ کی وجہ سے نقصان اٹھائے، اس فریق سے جس نے معاہدہ توڑا ہو، ایسے نقصان یا ضرر کے لیے جو اس وجہ سے اسے ہوا ہو، معاوضہ وصول کرنے کا حق رکھتا ہے

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
No, you are not entitled to hold the person liable for non-performance; rather, you are bound to compensate them for any loss caused by your failure to perform your part of the contract.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, if a contract consists of reciprocal promises and one party fails to perform their obligation (such as providing necessary materials or access), the other party is not required to perform their promise and is entitled to compensation for any loss sustained due to the non-performance.

citations.quote: When a contract consists of reciprocal promises, such that one of them cannot be performed, or that its performance cannot be claimed till the other has been performed, and the promisor of the promise last mentioned fails to perform it, such promisor cannot claim the performance of the reciprocal promise, and must make compensation to the other party to the contract for any loss which such other party may sustain by the non-performance of the contract.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found

Agar contract mein performance ki jagah tay nahi hai aur promisee ne koi darkhwast nahi ki, toh promisor ka farz hai ke woh promisee se rabta kare taake performance ke liye koi munasib jagah muqarrar ki ja sake.
answer.explanation: Contract Act ki Section 49 ke mutabiq, jab performance ke liye koi jagah muqarrar na ho aur promisee ki taraf se koi application na di gayi ho, toh promisor ki zimmedari hai ke woh promisee se munasib jagah muqarrar karne ki darkhwast kare aur phir wahin performance mukammal kare.

citations.quote: When a promise is to be performed without application by the promisee, and no place is fixed for the performance of it, it is the duty of the promisor to apply to the promisee to appoint a reasonable place for the performance of the promise, and to perform it at such place.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
In the absence of a contract to the contrary, co-sureties are liable to pay an equal share of the debt or the remaining unpaid portion.
answer.explanation: Co-sureties for the same debt are required to contribute equally among themselves unless they have entered into a specific agreement that dictates otherwise.

citations.quote: the co-sureties, in the absence of any contract to the contrary, are liable, as between themselves, to pay each an equal share of the whole debt, or of that part of it which remains unpaid by the principal debtor.

answer.short_answer: عوامی راستے پر لاپرواہی سے گاڑی چلانے کی صورت میں دو سال تک قید، تین ہزار روپے تک جرمانہ، یا دونوں سزائیں ہو سکتی ہیں۔
answer.explanation: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کی دفعہ 279 کے تحت، عوامی راستے پر اس قدر لاپرواہی یا غفلت سے گاڑی چلانا جس سے انسانی زندگی کو خطرہ ہو یا کسی کو چوٹ پہنچنے کا امکان ہو، ایک قابل سزا جرم ہے۔

citations.quote: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 2[two years] or with fine which may extend to 1[three] thousand rupees, or with both.

answer.short_answer: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کی دفعہ 357 کے تحت، کسی شخص کو غلط طریقے سے قید کرنے کی کوشش میں حملہ کرنے یا مجرمانہ طاقت استعمال کرنے کی سزا ایک سال تک قید، یا تین ہزار روپے تک جرمانہ، یا دونوں ہو سکتی ہے۔
answer.explanation: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کی دفعہ 357 واضح کرتی ہے کہ جو کوئی بھی کسی شخص کو غلط طریقے سے قید کرنے کی کوشش میں اس پر حملہ کرے یا مجرمانہ طاقت کا استعمال کرے، اسے مذکورہ بالا سزا دی جائے گی۔

citations.quote: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting wrongfully to confine that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to 3[three thousand rupees], or with both.

answer.short_answer: A person who advocates for the abolition of Pakistan's sovereignty may be punished with rigorous imprisonment for up to ten years and a fine.
answer.explanation: Under the Pakistan Penal Code, it is an offense to advocate for the curtailment or abolition of Pakistan's sovereignty, or to condemn the creation of Pakistan, if done with the intent or likelihood of influencing the public in a manner prejudicial to the safety or ideology of the country.

citations.quote: advocate the curtailment or abolition of the sovereignty of Pakistan in respect of all or any of the territories lying within its borders, whether by amalgamation with the territories of neighboring States or otherwise, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.

answer.short_answer: Yes, an individual can be charged with cheating by personation even if the person they are pretending to be is imaginary.
answer.explanation: According to the Pakistan Penal Code, the offence of cheating by personation is committed regardless of whether the person being impersonated is a real or an imaginary person.

citations.quote: The offence is committed whether the in dividual personated is a real or imaginary person.

answer.short_answer: Under Section 337Q of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, the arsh for causing the destruction (itlaf) of an organ found singly in the human body is equivalent to the value of diyat.
answer.explanation: Section 337Q specifically addresses organs that exist singly in the human body, such as the nose or tongue, and mandates that the compensation (arsh) for their destruction must be equal to the value of diyat.

citations.quote: The arsh for causing itlaf of an organ which is found singly in a human body shall be equivalent to the value of diyat.

answer.short_answer: An intoxicated person who causes annoyance in a public place may be punished with simple imprisonment for up to twenty-four hours, a fine of up to thirty rupees, or both.
answer.explanation: Under Section 510 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, any person who appears in a public place while intoxicated and conducts themselves in a manner that causes annoyance to others is subject to these specific penalties.

citations.quote: Whoever, in a state of intoxication appears in any public place, or in any place which it is a trespass in him to enter, and there conducts himself in such a manner as to cause annoyance to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to twenty-four hours, or with fine which may extend to 1[thirty] rupees, or with both.

answer.short_answer: The maximum term of imprisonment for causing mudihah to another person is five years.
answer.explanation: Under the Pakistan Penal Code, an offender who causes mudihah is liable to daman and may be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to five years as ta'zir.

citations.quote: (iv) mudihah to any person, shall be liable to daman and may also be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years as ta'zir

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
No sufficient source found
Yes, it is a criminal offense to accept gratification as a motive or reward for inducing a public servant to perform an official act through the exercise of personal influence.
answer.explanation: Under the Pakistan Penal Code, any person who accepts, obtains, or attempts to obtain gratification for themselves or others as a reward for using personal influence to induce a public servant to perform or refrain from an official act is subject to punishment, which may include imprisonment for up to one year, a fine, or both.

citations.quote: Whoever accepts or obtains, or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain, from any person, for himself or for any other person, any gratification whatever, as a motive or reward for in ducing, by the exercise of personal influence, any public servant to do or to forbear to do any official act... shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, National Assembly ke dissolve hone ki surat mein Federal Government kharchon ke liye funds authorize kar sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Aaeen-e-Pakistan ke mutabiq, jab National Assembly dissolve ho jaye to Federal Government Federal Consolidated Fund se kisi bhi mali saal mein char mah se zyada arsay ke liye nahi, balkay us arsay ke liye ikhrajat authorize kar sakti hai jab tak Article 82 ke tehat grants ki voting aur Article 83 ke tehat schedule of authorized expenditure ki takmeel na ho jaye.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing provisions relating to financial matters, at any time when the National Assembly stands dissolved, the Federal Government may authorize expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund in respect of the estimated expenditure for a period not exceeding four months in any financial year

answer.short_answer: If a member of a Provincial Assembly is appointed as Governor, their seat in the Assembly becomes vacant on the day they enter upon their office.
answer.explanation: According to the Constitution, a Governor cannot be a member of a Provincial Assembly, and the seat of any such member appointed as Governor is vacated upon their assumption of the office of Governor.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: if a member of 1[Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)] or a Provincial Assembly is appointed as Governor, his seat in 1[Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)] or, as the case may be, the Provincial Assembly shall become vacant on the day he enters upon his office.

answer.short_answer: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 ke Article 203F ke tehat, Federation ya Province ke liye appeal karne ki muddat che (6) mahine hai.
answer.explanation: Article 203F(1) ke mutabiq, aam taur par appeal 60 din mein ki ja sakti hai, lekin Federation ya Province ke liye yeh muddat barha kar che mahine kar di gayi hai.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: Provided that an appeal on behalf of the Federation or of a Province may be preferred within six months of such decision.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
No, a court cannot validate an act of high treason against the Constitution.
answer.explanation: The Constitution explicitly prohibits any court, including the Federal Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court, and any High Court, from validating acts of high treason as defined in Article 6.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: An act of high treason mentioned in clause (1) or clause (2) shall not be validated by any court including the Federal Constitutional Court, Supreme Court and a High Court.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
Ji haan, Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ki Section 39(2) ke mutabiq, court khud se (of its own motion) kisi decree ko execution ke liye kisi subordinate court ko transfer kar sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Section 39(2) wazeh taur par bayan karti hai ke jis court ne decree pass ki ho, woh apni marzi se (suo motu) ise execution ke liye kisi aisi subordinate court ko bhej sakti hai jo is mamlay ki samaat ki ahal ho.

citations.quote: The Court which passed a decree may of its own motion send it for execution to any subordinate Court of competent jurisdiction.

answer.short_answer: No, a public officer is generally exempt from arrest and the attachment of their property during a lawsuit concerning their official duties, except in the execution of a decree.
answer.explanation: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a public officer sued for acts done in their official capacity cannot be arrested, nor can their property be attached, unless it is done to execute a court decree.

citations.quote: the defendant shall not be liable to arrest nor his property to attachment otherwise than in execution of a decree

جی ہاں، کوڈ آف سول پروسیجر 1908 کی سیکشن 86A کے تحت مخصوص حالات میں سفارتی نمائندے کے خلاف قانونی کارروائی کی جا سکتی ہے۔
answer.explanation: سفارتی نمائندے کے خلاف کارروائی تب ممکن ہے جب معاملہ ان کی نجی غیر منقولہ جائیداد، ان کی ذاتی حیثیت میں وراثت، یا پاکستان میں ان کے سرکاری فرائض سے ہٹ کر کسی تجارتی یا پیشہ ورانہ سرگرمی سے متعلق ہو۔

citations.quote: No proceeding in any Court shall lie against a diplomatic agent except in a case relating to__ (a) any private immoveable property situated in Pakistan held by him in his private capacity and not on behalf of the sending State for the purpose of the mission ; (b) a succession in which the diplomatic agent is involved as executor, administrator, heir or legatee as a private person and not on behalf of the sending State; (c) any professional or commercial activity exercised by the diplomatic agent in Pakistan outside his official functions.

answer.short_answer: Yes, a High Court may order the execution of a decree before the costs are ascertained, provided the execution excludes the portion related to costs until they are taxed.
answer.explanation: If a High Court deems it necessary, it can order the immediate execution of a decree passed in its original civil jurisdiction, excluding the costs. The portion of the decree relating to costs may then be executed once the amount has been ascertained through taxation.

citations.quote: Where any High Court considers it necessary that a decree passed in the exercise of its original civil jurisdiction should be executed before the amount of the costs incurred in the suit can be ascertained by taxation, the Court may order that the decree shall be executed forthwith, except as to so much thereof as relates to the costs

answer.short_answer: Yes, the court has the discretion to allow you to pay the deficient court fees at any stage of the proceedings.
answer.explanation: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the court is empowered to permit the payment of any unpaid court fees at any stage, and once paid, the document is treated as if the fees had been paid initially.

citations.quote: the Court may, in its discretion, at any stage, allow the person, by whom such fee is payable, to pay the whole or part, as the case may be, of such court-fee; and upon such payment the document, in respect of which such fee is payable, shall have the same force and effect as if such fee had been paid in the first instance.

answer.short_answer: Income derived from a business or source that has ceased is treated as if the business or source had not ceased at the time the income was derived.
answer.explanation: Under Section 72, if income is derived from a source that ceased before or during the tax year, and that income would have been chargeable to tax had the source not ceased, the Ordinance applies as if the source were still active.

citations.quote: this Ordinance shall apply to the income on the basis that the business, activity, investment or other source had not ceased at the time the income was derived.

answer.short_answer: No, two individuals cannot be considered associates solely because they are both employees of the same company.
answer.explanation: The Income Tax Ordinance explicitly states that two persons shall not be treated as associates merely because they are both employees of a third person.

citations.quote: Two persons shall not be associates solely by reason of the fact that one person is an employee of the other or both persons are employees of a third person.

answer.short_answer: No, mutual funds and insurance companies are not subject to the same capital gain tax computation rules as other entities under Section 100B.
answer.explanation: While Section 100B generally mandates that capital gains on listed securities be computed according to the Eighth Schedule, it explicitly excludes mutual funds and insurance companies from these provisions. Instead, these entities must compute capital gains using the mechanism prescribed under Section 37A and deposit tax according to the applicable provisions of the Ordinance.

citations.quote: The provisions of sub–section (1) shall not apply to the following persons or class of persons, namely:- (a) a mutual fund; banking company and an insurance company subject to tax under the Fourth Schedule

NCCPL, in case of banking company, insurance company and mutual funds, shall compute and determine the capital gain as per the mechanism prescribed under section 37A; however, these entities shall continue to deposit tax on the amount of capital gain as per the applicable provisions of this Ordinance.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
Ji haan, agar aap kisi shakhs par terrorism ka shaq karte hain, to aap police officer ko iski itla de sakte hain.
answer.explanation: Qanoon ke mutabiq, koi bhi shakhs police officer par apna shaq ya yaqeen zahir kar sakta hai ke koi shakhs dehshat gardi se mutaliq sargarmiyon mein mulawis hai ya dehshat gardi se hasil shuda maal ya jaidad rakhta hai.

citations.quote: کوئی شخص پولیس افسر پر: (الف) یہ شک یا یقین ظاہر کر سکتا ہے کہ کوئی شخص رقم یا دیگر جائیداد دہشت گردی جائیداد یا ملکیت ہے یا دہشت گردی سے ملنے والی جائیداد ہے حاصل کر رکھے ؛ یا (ب) ایسا مواد یا جو شک پر مبنی ہو

answer.short_answer: A person sentenced by an Anti-terrorism Court must file an appeal to the High Court within fifteen days of the passing of the sentence.
answer.explanation: According to the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, the statutory time limit for a convicted person to prefer an appeal against their sentence is fifteen days from the date the sentence is passed.

citations.quote: An appeal under sub-section (1) may be preferred by a person sentenced by 1[an Anti- terrorismCourt] to 1[a High Court] within 2[fifteen] days of the passing of the sentence.

If a wife exercises a delegated right to divorce or if parties seek to dissolve a marriage through means other than talaq, the provisions of Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, apply mutatis mutandis.
answer.explanation: The law mandates that for any dissolution of marriage occurring outside of the standard talaq process, the procedural requirements set forth in Section 7 (which include providing written notice to the Chairman and a copy to the other spouse) must be followed as far as they are applicable.

citations.quote: Where the right to divorce has been duly delegated to the wife and she wishes to exercise that right, or where any of the parties to a marriage wishes to dissolve the marriage otherwise than by talaq, the provisions of section 7 shall, mutatis mutandis and so far as applicable, apply.

answer.short_answer: Agar Union Council ka Chairman non-Muslim ho, toh Arbitration Council apne Muslim members mein se kisi ek ko Chairman muntakhib (elect) karegi.
answer.explanation: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance ke mutabiq, agar Union Council ka Chairman non-Muslim ho, toh Arbitration Council ke maqasid ke liye Council apne Muslim members mein se kisi ek ko Chairman muntakhib karti hai.

citations.quote: Provided that where the Chairman of the Union Council is a non- Muslim, or he himself wishes to make an application to the Arbitration Council, or is, owing to illness or any other reason, unable to discharge the functions of Chairman, the Council shall elect one of its Muslim members as Chairman for the purposes of this Ordinance

answer.short_answer: جی ہاں، اینٹی منی لانڈرنگ ایکٹ 2010 کے تحت وفاقی حکومت کو اس ایکٹ کے نفاذ میں پیش آنے والی مشکلات کو دور کرنے کا اختیار حاصل ہے۔
answer.explanation: اگر اس ایکٹ کے نفاذ کے دوران کوئی مشکل پیدا ہو تو وفاقی حکومت سرکاری گزٹ میں حکم جاری کر کے ایسی دفعات بنا سکتی ہے جو اس ایکٹ کے منافی نہ ہوں اور مشکل کو دور کرنے کے لیے ضروری ہوں۔

citations.quote: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Federal Government may, by order, published in the official Gazette, make such provisions not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act as may appear to be necessary for removing the difficulty.

answer.short_answer: If immediate action is required, an investigating officer may conduct a search and seizure with the prior permission of a senior officer of the concerned agency who is not below the rank of BS-20.
answer.explanation: Under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010, while search powers generally require court permission, a proviso to Section 14 allows for immediate action to be taken with the authorization of a senior officer of at least BS-20 rank. Additionally, the investigating officer must forward a report of the search and seizure to the head of the agency within forty-eight hours.

citations.quote: Provided that where immediate action is required, the powers of search and seizure shall be exercisable with prior permission of senior officer of the concerned investigating or prosecuting agency not below the rank of an officer of BS-20.

The investigating officer shall, within forty-eight hours immediately after search and seizure, forward a copy of the report on search and seizure to the head of the concerned investigating or prosecuting agency in a sealed envelope.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, BS-17 aur us se upar ke civil servants ki assets ki details public ke liye available hoti hain.
answer.explanation: Civil Servants Act, 1973 ke mutabiq, BS-17 aur us se upar ke civil servants, unke spouse aur dependent children ki assets ki tafseelat Federal Board of Revenue ke paas digitally file ki jati hain aur ye tafseelat FBR ke zariye public ke liye available hoti hain.

citations.quote: the declaration of assets of a Civil Servant of BS-17 and above, his spouse and dependent children, including domestic and foreign assets and liabilities, as may be prescribed, shall be digitally filed with the Federal Board of Revenue and same shall be publicly available, through Federal Board of Revenue, in accordance with the rules as may be prescribed

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found

Federal Board of Revenue Act, 2007, Section 19 ke tehat, Board taxpayers ko behtar sahuliyat faraham karne ke akhrajat, direct cost reimbursement, aur public-private partnership ke tehat fiscal laws se mutaliq khidmat faraham karne par munasib munafa ya investment par return ke liye fees ya charges laga sakta hai.
answer.explanation: Section 19 Board ko ikhtiyar deta hai ke woh taxpayers ke liye enhanced facilities, kharchon ki wapsi, aur public-private partnership ke zariye di gayi khidmat par fees ya charges wasool kar sake.

citations.quote: The Board may levy any fee or charges for making expenditure on the provision of enhanced facilities for the taxpayers, or direct cost reimbursement of expenses, and reasonable return on investment or profit; where services are provided in the matters relating to or under any fiscal law under public-private partnership.

answer.short_answer: The Appellate Authority is required to pass appropriate orders on an employee's appeal within ninety days of receiving the application.
answer.explanation: Under the National Command Authority Act, 2010, an employee aggrieved by matters concerning their terms and conditions of service may appeal to the Appellate Authority, which must decide the matter within ninety days of receipt.

citations.quote: The Appellate Authority may provide personal hearing to the applicant and pass appropriate orders within ninety days of the receipt of application.

answer.short_answer: The Provincial Government argued that the 2001 Ordinance redefined "licensee" to include persons generating electricity for self-use with generators over 500 KW, thereby withdrawing previous protections and making them liable for electricity duty under section 13.
answer.explanation: The Provincial Government contended that the 2001 Ordinance fundamentally changed the legal position, statutorily classifying these entities as licensees and thus subjecting them to the electricity duty imposed by section 13 of the relevant law.

citations.act_or_case: Govt. of Punjab v. M/s. Kunjah Textile Mills Ltd.
citations.quote: In terms of the last portion thereof (“any person generating the electric power from a generator having the capacity of more than five hundred kilowatt for self use”) they statutorily became licensees. Any protection that they may have had in terms of the 1985 notification stood withdrawn by the 2001 notification and thus they were liable to pay the electricity duty imposed by s. 13.

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne Tribunal ke us faislay ko ghalat qarar diya jis mein 2015 se tamam promotions ki scrutiny aur reversion ka hukam diya gaya tha, kyunke yeh Tribunal ke ikhtiyar-e-samaat se bahar tha aur is mein mutasireen ko sunne ka moqa nahi diya gaya tha.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne note kiya ke Tribunal ne suo moto powers ka istemal karte hue 2015 se tamam promotions ko revert karne ka jo hukam diya, woh na sirf administrative bohran ka sabab bana balkay yeh natural justice ke usoolon (right of audience) ki khilaf warzi thi kyunke mutasireen ko notice nahi diya gaya tha.

citations.quote: The directions issued for scrutinizing and reversion of all promotions across all MTIs since 2015, is not only harsh but as a matter of fact, such relief was neither sought by the appellants before the learned Tribunal nor any such claim or prayer was the subject matter of appeals.
The principles of natural justice and fair-mindedness are grounded in the philosophy of affording a right of audience before any detrimental action is taken

The order of the scrutiny and reversion of all promotions across all MTIs since 2015 was passed even without issuing notice to the affectees which blatantly violated the right to fair trial and due process.

answer.short_answer: Trial Court ne mulzim ko saza-e-maut sunayi aur 200,000 rupay harjana ada karne ka hukum diya, jis ki adaigi na karne ki surat mein usay chhay mahine ki qaid-e-ba-mashaqqat bhugatni thi.
answer.explanation: Trial Court ne mulzim ko section 302(b) PPC ke tehat qatal ka mujrim qarar dete hue saza-e-maut sunayi aur warisan ko 200,000 rupay harjana ada karne ka hukum diya, jis ki adam adaigi par chhay mahine ki qaid-e-ba-mashaqqat ki saza muqarrar ki.

citations.quote: the Trial Court convicted the petitioner under section 302(b) PPC for the murder of Muhammad Tufail (deceased) and sentenced him to death with an order to pay Rs.200,000/- as compensation to the legal heirs of the deceased and in default whereof to undergo six months S.I.

Police authorities are legally obligated to immediately execute an arrest once a court dismisses a pre-arrest bail application, without waiting for further instructions or assuming a stay exists.
answer.explanation: Investigating officers must act promptly and in good faith to enforce judicial orders, as the dismissal of pre-arrest bail signifies that the accused is subject to lawful arrest. The mere filing of a petition in a higher forum does not operate as an automatic stay or a shield against arrest unless an express injunctive order is granted by a competent court.

citations.act_or_case: Zahid Khan, etc v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another
citations.quote: This Court, therefore, finds it imperative to state clearly that investigating officers and police authorities are legally bound to act upon court orders dismissing pre-arrest bail immediately, without waiting for further instructions or presuming the existence of any stay where none has been granted.

citations.act_or_case: Zahid Khan, etc v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another
citations.quote: Absent such an order, a refusal of bail remains fully operative and must be implemented promptly and in good faith by investigating authorities.

answer.short_answer: The Court must be satisfied that the defendant is intentionally avoiding service or that the summons cannot be served through ordinary means.
answer.explanation: Before ordering substituted service, the Court must have reason to believe the defendant is keeping out of the way to avoid service or that ordinary service is not possible.

citations.quote: Where the Court is satisfied that there is reason to believe that the defendant is keeping out of the way for the purpose of avoiding service, or that for any other reason the summons cannot be served in the ordinary way, the Court shall order for service of summons

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court held that a cheque payment alone is not conclusive proof of a valid sale transaction when transferring property to an attorney's sons, especially without an agreement to sell or other independent evidence.
answer.explanation: The Court determined that producing a cheque payment without establishing the underlying transaction or providing corroborative evidence fails to meet the legal standard required to validate the alienation of immovable property, particularly when the transfer is made to the attorney's own relatives without the principal's express consent.

citations.act_or_case: Javed Iqbal & others v. Mst. Farhat Iqbal (deceased) through LRs
citations.quote: The alleged payment through cheque, made by the appellant (brother) in favour of the respondent (sister), is not conclusive proof of a valid sale transaction, particularly in the absence of any agreement to sell or other independent corroborative evidence reflecting a lawful bargain. Mere production of such payment, without establishing the underlying transaction, does not satisfy the legal standard required to validate an alienation of immovable property.

answer.short_answer: Under the 2001 Ordinance, a failure to collect advance tax when required makes a person a deemed taxpayer in default, which triggers Section 161 and activates Section 163.
answer.explanation: According to the Department's position, if a person required to collect advance tax fails to do so, they are considered a deemed taxpayer in default under Section 161. This triggers Section 163, which mandates that the provisions of the Ordinance apply to the required amount as if it were tax due under an assessment order, leading to severe penal consequences.

citations.quote: This alleged failure, according to the Department, triggered s. 161 of the 2001 Ordinance which, inter alia, applies when a person who is required to deduct or collect advance tax fails to do so. Such failure makes that person a deemed taxpayer in default and, inter alia, activates s. 163 which provides as follows: “The provisions of this Ordinance shall apply to any amount required to be paid to the Commissioner under this Division as if it were tax due under an assessment order”.

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court of Pakistan ruled that the forfeiture of the performance guarantee by the Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) was justified and set aside the lower courts' orders directing its refund.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court allowed TCP's appeal, determining that the forfeiture of the performance guarantee was reasonable under the circumstances, thereby overturning the previous judgments of the Sindh High Court that had ordered the refund.

citations.act_or_case: Trading Corporation of Pakistan v. M/s
citations.quote: The forfeiture of the entire amount of the performance guarantee by TCP was justified and reasonable in the facts and circumstances of the case. ... The judgments of the learned Single Judge and the Division Bench of the Sindh High Court, insofar as they direct refund of the performance guarantee, are hereby set aside.

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne observe kiya ke agar petitioner (baap) apni beti ke khilaf maintenance ka suit wapas nahi leta, toh Court apne faislay par nazar-e-sani (review) karegi.

citations.act_or_case: Sadiq Subhani v. Sadia Arooj and others
citations.quote: In the event the suit is not withdrawn by the petitioner, this fact would cause us to review our judgment.

answer.short_answer: The primary legal controversy concerns the allocation of reserved seats for women and non-Muslims to political parties in the National and Provincial Assemblies in accordance with the Constitution.
answer.explanation: The core issue involves determining whether the allocation of these seats aligns with the principle of proportional representation as mandated by the Constitution, specifically regarding whether parties received seats exceeding their numerical strength or if seats should be left vacant.

citations.quote: The core controversy requiring resolution relates to the allocation of reserved seats for women and non-Muslims to political parties in the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies in accordance with Article 51(6)(d) and (e) and Article 106(3)(c) of the Constitution, respectively.
the learned counsel argued, was a blatant violation of the principle of proportional representation enshrined in Article 51(6)(d) and (e) and Article 106(3)(c) of the Constitution.

answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne note kiya hai ke High Court of Sindh ki 7 November 2024 ki judgment mein un cases ki tafseelat di gayi hain jo wukala ne apne clients ke khilaf darj karwaye hain, aur is trend ko fori tawajjo ka mustahiq samjha gaya hai.

citations.act_or_case: Syed Basit Hyder Taqvi v. The State
citations.quote: The judgment details the cases lodged by the Advocates against their clients, indicating the aforementioned trend. This is a significant development that necessitates immediate attention.

answer.short_answer: The accused, Allah Yar, filed an application for a medical board before the Area Magistrate, which was initially dismissed, but subsequently allowed by the Additional Sessions Judge in a revision petition.
answer.explanation: In the case involving FIR No. 379/2026, the accused Allah Yar applied to the Area Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala, to constitute a medical board for specific Medico-Legal Examination Certificates. The Magistrate dismissed this application on May 21, 2026. Following this, Allah Yar filed a revision petition, which the Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala, allowed on June 15, 2026.

citations.quote: Allah Yar (mentioned above) filed application before learned Area Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala for constituting medical board regarding Medico-Legal Examination Certificates... which was dismissed vide order dated: 21.05.2026 passed by learned Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala... answer.short_answer: Lahore High Court ne acquired land ka compensation Rs. 5,00,000/- per marla ke uniform rate par tay kiya.
answer.explanation: Court ne yeh faisla land ki location, potential, aur us waqt ke prevailing market conditions ko madd-e-nazar rakhte hue kiya, kyunke pehle se diye gaye rates (front aur rear ke liye alag alag) sahi market value ki akasi nahi kar rahe thay.

citations.quote: Keeping in view the totality of circumstances, the location and potential of the acquired land, the prevailing market conditions at the relevant time and the judicial precedents referred to hereinabove, we are of the considered opinion that the ends of justice would be adequately met by assessing the entire land at a uniform rate of Rs.5,00,000/- per marla.

answer.short_answer: The Lahore High Court suggested allowing the petitioner to withdraw the suit and file a fresh one on the same cause of action by impleading the necessary parties.
answer.explanation: The Court determined that when necessary parties are missing, it may allow the withdrawal of the suit with permission to file a new one on the same cause of action, a course of action to which both parties consented.

citations.quote: In view thereof, the alternate procedure available before this Court for reaching just conclusion of the matter would be to allow the petitioner to withdraw the suit and file afresh one on the basis of same cause of action by impleading necessary parties referred to in the judgments passed by the courts below. When confronted, both the sides have no objection to the said course of action.

answer.short_answer: The court erred by declaring the girl a child under sixteen years of age and ordering her detention without her consent.
answer.explanation: The court wrongly invoked the Punjab Child Marriage Restraint Act 2026 and section 552 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C) to order the detention of the girl, despite her stating that she was sui juris and had married of her own free will.

citations.act_or_case: Sher Baz etc v. Ahmad Sher etc
citations.quote: Court kept pending proceedings till 20.05.2026 and on said date, culminated proceedings by declaring her “Child” under sixteen years of age by wrongly invoking “The Punjab Child Marriage Restraint Act 2026” (hereinafter the Act 2026) as well as applying Rule nisi in habeas corpus as no such powers available under section 552 Cr.P.C to pass order of detention

answer.short_answer: Yes, a person who provides necessaries to someone incapable of contracting is entitled to be reimbursed from that individual's property.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, if a person who is incapable of entering into a contract, or someone they are legally bound to support, is supplied with necessaries suited to their condition in life, the supplier has a legal right to be reimbursed from the property of the incapable person.

citations.quote: If a person, incapable of entering into a contract, or any one whom he is legally bound to support, is supplied by another person with necessaries suited to his condition in life, the person who has furnished such supplies is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of such incapable person.

Supreme Court ne High Court ke faislay ko kaladam qarar detay huay mamlay ko dobara faislay ke liye wapis bhej diya hai taake High Court az-sar-e-nau aur azadana taur par concurrent findings ka jaiza le sakay.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne note kiya ke High Court ko rent laws (SRPO) ke tehat concurrent findings ko set aside karne ke mamlay par dobara ghor karne ki zaroorat hai. Is liye, Supreme Court ne High Court ke faislay ko set aside kar diya aur mamlay ko 6 mahine ke andar fresh adjudication ke liye wapis bhej diya.

citations.quote: In view of the foregoing, certain crucial points falling within the jurisdictional ambit of the rent laws (SRPO), particularly those relating to the setting aside of concurrent findings recorded by the two courts below in writ jurisdiction under the special law, require reconsideration in order to arrive at a proper conclusion. Accordingly, this Civil Petition is converted into an appeal and allowed. Consequently, the impugned judgment of the High Court is set aside, and the matter is remanded for fresh adjudication to the High Court with independent application of mind, preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of this judgment.
